reader.requirement: GR1 is a presentation pointer: the RD admits the CODE, CONTROL and PAGE clauses (each specified by its own clause from XIII-14 on), and with SR2 they may follow report-name-1 in any order, each once; the compiler must accept every order and give each clause its own semantics.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 refuses the identifier-1 operand (COBOL2713); 2002+ accepts it
below 2002 literal-1 must be exactly two characters (1985 SR1); 2002+ any length
ConstructRegistry report-code-is-2002: the word IS after CODE refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)
CODE reserved at all four editions
2002 PAGE forms (LAST CONTROL HEADING, COLUMNS) refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the CODE clause is CODE literal-1 (no IS, no identifier, two characters) and the PAGE clause lacks LAST CH / COLUMNS; the clause ordering itself is edition-neutral (grammar reportDescriptionClause*, binder UnrepeatedElements)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness writes CODE alone; CODE/CONTROL/PAGE together in a non-alphabetical order and a repeated clause are not exercised

probes.printed: RD with PAGE, then CONTROL, then CODE "Q7" accepted; L01 [Q7  PH] L02 [Q7DET 1  02] L03 [Q7DET 2  03] L04 [Q7CF] L05 [Q7DET 3  05] <FF> L06 [Q7  PH] L07 [Q7DET 4  02] L08 [Q7CF]
probes.expected: order immaterial (SR2); each clause takes effect

probes.printed: COBOL2423 RD 'R-A': the CODE clause is written 2 times
probes.expected: each clause a bracket written once

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the LAST CONTROL HEADING phrase of the PAGE clause requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused: not in the 1985 PAGE format

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the page width (COLS or COLUMNS) requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused: not in the 1985 PAGE format

reader.notes: The rule places no behaviour of its own; it is decided by showing the three clauses are accepted at 85 in a non-alphabetical order with their effects intact, a repeat is refused, and 2002-only phrases inside them are refused.

refuter.evidence: r1order.cob (refute-1985-038/r1order-001): two RDs on one file; R-A written CONTROLS ARE FINAL WS-K, CODE "AA", PAGE 8 with no LIMIT/LINES word and the PAGE phrases in the order FOOTING, LAST DETAIL, HEADING, FIRST DETAIL; R-B written PAGE LIMITS ARE 5 LINE, CODE, CONTROL IS. Output: R-A PH 1, D A 2-3, CF 4, D B 5-6, page advance (6+1>LD 6), PH 1, D B 2, CF 3, CZ 4; R-B E 1-2, CB 3, E 4-5, page advance, E 1, CB 2; every record carries its report's code. Each clause took its own effect in every order. Refusals: r1big PAGE 1000 LINES -> COBOL2744 (SR2 of PAGE); r1dup two PAGE clauses -> COBOL2423; r1ctl CONTROL then CONTROLS -> COBOL2423. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.5.4 GR1; OK §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2; OK §1985:XIII.3.8.3 SR1. The IPC format (X-22, 4.4.2) adds only IS GLOBAL, which the reader's p11glob already ran.
